subject: Problem combining imaging runs after mzBin

messages.author: 71755fba910dfee9
messages.subject: Problem combining imaging runs after mzBin
parts:
Hello again,

Apologies in advance for all my recent questions but this group has been so helpful in helping me figure out Cardinal. 

As some other users have mentioned, I too have problems combining multiple datasets. I see a number of people suggest to use mzBin on the datasets you want to combine to make them have the same mz values, then combine the binned files. In my case even after I use mzBin, when I try to combine them I get the error
"Error in combine_by_cols(...) : number of rows of matrices must match"

The code I am using is:
NHL114_binned <- mzBin(NHL114, from=min(mz(NHL114)), to=max(mz(NHL114)),
                       resolution = NA, units ="mz", fun=sum)
process(NHL114_binned)

NHL115_binned <- mzBin(NHL115, from=min(mz(NHL115)), to=max(mz(NHL115)),
                       resolution = NA, units ="mz", fun=sum)
process(NHL115_binned)

data_combined_binned <- Cardinal::combine(NHL114_binned, NHL115_binned)  

where NHL114 and NHL115 are separate imzML files that I would like to combine.

If anyone has any suggestions as to where I am going wrong I would be really grateful.:)

Many thanks,
Sandra

messages.author: db2a70d9b31cb1f7
messages.subject: Re: Problem combining imaging runs after mzBin
parts:
Hi Sandra,

you might want to check your Cardinal version. Cardinal::combine is deprecated and replaced by cbind()
-> maybe you have already success with data_combined_binned <- cbind(NHL114_binned, NHL115_binned)

The aim of the binning is to obtain the same mz axis for all files. Therefore, you should set "from" and "to" to the mz range that is shared by all files,e.g:
file1: 799.9300 - 2999.9800
file2: 799.9100 - 2999.9500
--> from=799.9300, to=2999.9500 OR from=800, to=2999
Within this shared mz range you want to obtain the same mz bins for each file, therefore it might be necessary to set "resolution" to an exact value instead of NA, because the latter results in an estimation of an appropriate bin size that could be different for different files. At this step you normally want to keep the bin size as small as possible and close to the original bin size, so the optimal bin size results in a similar amount of mz values as you have in the original file. Cardinal gives you a warning in case your chosen bin size is smaller than in the original file, I normally try to just be a tiny bit larger than the original bin size to not get a warning but keep as much information as possible during this step.

Best,
Melanie

messages.author: db2a70d9b31cb1f7
messages.subject: Re: Problem combining imaging runs after mzBin
parts:
Hi Sandra,

to check if the mz axis are exactly the same you can use: all.equal(mz(file1), mz(file2)) --> TRUE means that both files have exactly the same mz values and can be combined.
Maybe you forget to run process()? By default the pre-processing methods only run with the process() command:
mse_bin <- mzBin(mse_pre, from=1000, to=1600, resolution=1000, units="ppm")
mse_bin <- process(mse_bin)

Best,
Melanie
